fields.label: Gross profit (USD)
fields.formula: IF(OR({Status} = "Returned to stock", {Status} = "Transferred out"), "", {Patient copay (USD)} + {Plan paid (USD)} - {Acquisition cost (USD)})

fields.label: Margin (%)
fields.formula: IF(OR({Status} = "Returned to stock", {Status} = "Transferred out"), "", IF({Patient copay (USD)} + {Plan paid (USD)} > 0, ROUND({Gross profit (USD)} / ({Patient copay (USD)} + {Plan paid (USD)}) * 100, 0), 0))

fields.label: Margin check
fields.formula: IF(OR({Status} = "Returned to stock", {Status} = "Transferred out"), "", IF({Margin (%)} < 0, "Below cost", IF({Margin (%)} < 10, "Thin, brand", "Healthy")))

pages.title: Start here: how this workspace runs

text.text: This workspace follows one prescription from the moment it arrives to the moment the patient walks out, and keeps the shelf and the plan rejects in step with it.
The four tables
Prescriptions

is the fill queue. A new e-script, a phoned refill or a transfer comes in as New. It moves to Filling once data entry is done, to Ready for pickup once the pharmacist has verified it and it is bagged with a bin number, and to Picked up when it leaves. Mark picked up stamps the day.
Patients
holds the profile: plan, allergies, med sync day and whether they are on the delivery route. Each patient shows open prescriptions, bags waiting and lifetime gross profit.
Drug inventory
is every stocked item with its NDC, units on hand, reorder point, cost per unit and nearest expiry. Reorder check says Order now when on-hand falls to the reorder point.
Prior auths and rejects
catches every claim the plan refused at the counter, with the reject code and a follow-up date.
A normal day
Before opening, a technician works the Overdue and This week views on Prescriptions. Anything promised for yesterday and still not bagged is first.
Rejects from the overnight refills go straight to Prior auths and rejects. Start a prior auth from the prescription row so the two stay linked.
The pharmacist verifies Filling rows in promised order and presses Ready for pickup.
At 2 pm the buyer opens the Order tonight list on the Dashboard and places the order before the wholesaler's cutoff.
At close, count the will-call bins against the Waiting in will-call list. A bag you cannot find is a problem today, not next week.
Who owns what

text.text: Money in plain words

Gross profit on a fill is the copay plus what the plan paid, less your acquisition cost. Generics usually earn most of the store's margin; brand fills often earn only a few dollars, which is why Thin, brand is a normal label and not an alarm. Below cost is the alarm: write down the plan and drug and raise it at the next contract review.

pages.title: Will-call bins and return to stock

text.text: A bag left in will-call is money the plan has paid you on loan. Most plans expect the claim reversed if the patient never picks up, usually within 10 to 14 days. This page is the routine that keeps the bins honest.
The rule
Every bag gets a bin number (A-01 to C-20) written in Will-call bin before it goes on the shelf.
Day 1: the patient gets a text that the prescription is ready.
Day 5: a person calls. A real voice catches the patient who forgot, or tells you they no longer need it.
Day 10: the bag comes back to stock. Press Return to stock on the prescription, reverse the claim, and put the medicine back in its original bottle with the lot and expiry.
Weekly bin sweep (Monday, 20 minutes)
Open Prescriptions and use the Ready for pickup column of the board.
Sort by Promised for, oldest first. Anything over ten days is pulled.
For each pulled bag: reverse the claim, press Return to stock, and add a line in the row's page: date, who pulled it and why.
Controlled medicines are returned with a second person present and logged the same day.
Refrigerated items are checked every day, not weekly; a pen left out of the fridge is waste, not stock.
Calling script
"Hi, this is Bramblewood Pharmacy. Your prescription has been ready since Thursday. We hold it ten days, so we will keep it until next Monday. Would you like us to deliver it instead?"
Offer delivery before you offer anything else. Patients on the delivery route are flagged on the Patients board.
Why it matters

cells.text: The plan claws it back at audit, often with a penalty
Bag returned without lot and expiry
The stock cannot be dispensed again
A missed dose and, often, a transfer to another store

pages.title: Working a reject or prior auth

text.text: A reject at the counter is not a no. Most are fixed in a day if the right person gets the right form. This page is how the counter turns a reject into a filled prescription without the patient waiting in the dark.
Read the reject code first

cells.text: The plan wants the prescriber to justify the drug
Send the plan's form to the prescriber's office
The drug is off the plan's list
Ask the prescriber for the covered alternative
Less than about 75 percent of the last supply used
Check for a dose change or lost supply; vacation overrides exist
Fill to the limit now, request an override for the rest
Pharmacist reviews and enters the override code

text.text: Steps
From the prescription, press Start a prior auth. The new row is linked to it and the patient.
Write the code and the plan's exact message in the row. Set Follow up on to tomorrow.
Tell the patient what happens next and when you will call. Never let them leave thinking the medicine is simply unavailable.
Send the request. Move the row to Sent to prescriber, then Submitted to plan once the office has sent it.
When the plan answers, press Mark approved or Mark denied. Both stamp Decided on.
Approved: refill the claim and move the prescription to Filling. Denied: call the prescriber with one covered alternative and its cash price.
Ten-minute daily review
Open the Overdue view. Every row there is a patient without medicine.
Anything Sent to prescriber for two days gets a phone call, not another fax.
Write the outcome in What happened, so the next person does not repeat the call.
Worked example

A semaglutide new start rejects with 75. The technician starts a prior auth, faxes the form with a note that the plan wants the latest A1c and weight, and sets Follow up on to tomorrow. The office sends notes that afternoon; the plan approves the next morning; Mark approved stamps the day and the pen is ordered for next-day delivery.
